mainTopic: Three sources that a leftover פסח becomes a שלמים; then the new פרק on where the grain for מנחות may come from, and whether the עומר and שתי הלחם may come from old grain.
overview: The amud opens by asking what one opinion learns from the פסוק "וזבחת פסח... צאן ובקר". The answer is רב נחמן's rule: a leftover פסח (מותר הפסח) is brought as a שלמים. The גמרא objects twice, because the same rule is also learned from אבוה דשמואל's פסוק and from "אם כבש" in a ברייתא. It answers that the three sources cover three different cases: both the day and the animal's first year have passed, only the day has passed, or neither has passed. A צריכותא shows why each case needs its own source. The פרק התודה היתה באה then ends with a הדרן. A new פרק opens with a משנה: grain for מנחות may come from anywhere and from any year's crop, except the עומר and שתי הלחם, which need new grain from ארץ ישראל. The best grain is preferred, but all of it is valid. The גמרא notes that a ברייתא disagrees and accepts old grain after the fact, defends that view against the words "ראשית" and "חדשה", and begins to define exactly what the two sides argue about, a point that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What does the other opinion learn from this verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the other side does with the פסוק "צאן ובקר" if it does not use it for the earlier teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does he do with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the other opinion learns from the verse "וזבחת פסח... צאן ובקר", since it does not use that verse for the earlier teaching. This is a setup question, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a basic rule: no word in the תורה is extra. If one opinion does not use this verse the way the other side did, it must use it for something else. The גמרא now wants to know what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? The usual question for what an opinion learns from a verse it does not use for the topic under discussion

phrases.english: What does he do with it?
phrases.notes: "It" means the פסוק "וזבחת פסח... צאן ובקר" that was discussed just before this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion by asking how the other opinion uses the verse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the other opinion learns from "צאן ובקר" in the פסח verse.

steps.title: The פסוק teaches that a leftover פסח is brought as a שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The verse is needed for רב נחמן's teaching, in the name of רבה בר אבוה: a leftover פסח is brought as a שלמים, which can come from cattle as well as sheep.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for the teaching of רב נחמן. רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: Where do we learn that a leftover פסח is offered as a שלמים? The פסוק says, "You shall slaughter the פסח to ה׳ your God, from sheep and cattle." But a פסח comes only from lambs and goats! So the verse must mean that a leftover פסח becomes an offering that can come from sheep and cattle, which is a שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the verse teaches רב נחמן's rule: an animal set aside for a פסח that was not used becomes a שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח can never come from cattle (בקר), so the word "בקר" in the verse seems strange. רבה בר אבוה says the verse is pointing to what happens to a leftover פסח: it becomes the kind of offering that can come from both sheep and cattle. That offering is a שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: A leftover פסח: an animal set aside for a פסח that ended up not being offered
Peace offering; it can come from sheep, goats or cattle
Flock (sheep and goats) and cattle
He needs it (for a different teaching)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic halacha the rest of the section is about: an unused פסח animal is not wasted, because it is offered as a שלמים.

phrases.english: He needs it for the teaching of Rav Naḥman,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: as Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
From where do we learn that a leftover Paschal offering is offered as a peace offering?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְזָבַחְתָּ פֶּסַח לַה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ צֹאן וּבָקָר״,
phrases.english: As it says: "You shall slaughter the Passover offering to the Lord your God, from the flock and the herd."
phrases.notes: דברים 16:2

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא אֵין פֶּסַח בָּא אֶלָּא מִן הַכְּבָשִׂים וּמִן הָעִזִּים!
phrases.english: But a Paschal offering comes only from lambs and goats!
Rather, it means that a leftover Paschal offering should become

phrases.aramaic: לְדָבָר הַבָּא מִן הַצֹּאן וּמִן הַבָּקָר.
phrases.english: an offering that comes from the flock and from the herd.
phrases.notes: That kind of offering is a שלמים, because it can come from either flock or cattle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse is used for רב נחמן's teaching that a leftover פסח is brought as a שלמים.

steps.title: Isn't this already learned from שמואל's father's verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: we do not need this verse, because אבוה דשמואל already learns the same rule from "אם מן הצאן קרבנו לזבח שלמים".
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really learn it from here? We learn it from the verse of אבוה דשמואל! It is written, "If his offering for a peace offering is from the flock." And אבוה דשמואל said: an offering that comes only from the flock (the פסח) will become a peace offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 2. The rule about a leftover פסח already has a different source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבוה דשמואל reads "from the flock... a peace offering" as talking about an offering that comes only from the flock, which is the פסח. The verse is telling us it becomes a שלמים. If that verse already teaches the rule, then רב נחמן's verse would be extra, so the answer in step 2 does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it learned from here? A challenge that the source given is not really the source
His offering

phrases.english: But is it learned from here?
It is learned from the verse of Shmuel's father,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״אִם מִן הַצֹּאן קׇרְבָּנוֹ לְזֶבַח שְׁלָמִים״,
phrases.english: as it is written: "If his offering for a peace offering is from the flock."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:6

phrases.english: And Shmuel's father said:

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר הַבָּא מִן הַצֹּאן יְהֵא לְזֶבַח שְׁלָמִים.
phrases.english: An offering that comes from the flock will become a peace offering.
phrases.notes: He means the פסח, which can only come from the flock.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that "צאן ובקר" is needed for the rule of a leftover פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule is already learned from "אם מן הצאן... לזבח שלמים", so the verse in step 2 would be extra.

steps.title: It comes from yet another place: the word 'lamb'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes further: the rule is learned from a third source, a ברייתא. It starts quoting it: the word "כבש" includes the פסח in the rule of the אליה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And still, do we learn it from here? We learn it from there! A ברייתא teaches: the word "lamb" comes to include the פסח in the rule of the fat tail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another objection: the rule has a different source in a ברייתא. It starts quoting that ברייתא here, and the rest of the quote comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns several things from the word "כבש" in the section about שלמים. Its first teaching is that a פסח also has its אליה burned on the altar, just like a שלמים. That first part is only background; the part that really matters for this challenge comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: And still: a second, stronger objection
It is learned from there, from a different source
To include
The fat tail of a sheep, which is burned on the altar

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop at the אליה line. It is not yet the source for a leftover פסח. That source is the next line of the ברייתא, "אם כבש".

phrases.english: And still, is it learned from here?
It is learned from there!
Isn't it taught in a baraita:
"Lamb" comes to include the Paschal offering in the rule of the fat tail.
phrases.notes: The verses about שלמים say "lamb" (ויקרא 3:7) and require the fat tail to go on the altar (ויקרא 3:9).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection on top of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: Again, the claim that "צאן ובקר" is the source for the leftover פסח rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא learns the rule from the word "כבש", so the verse in step 2 is not needed.

steps.title: The ברייתא: 'אם כבש' brings a leftover פסח under all the laws of שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: "אם כבש" includes a פסח whose first year has passed, and שלמים brought because of a פסח, in all the laws of שלמים: סמיכה, נסכים and תנופת חזה ושוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says "If a lamb," it comes to include a פסח whose year has passed, and peace offerings that come because of a פסח, in all the laws of peace offerings: they need hands pressed on them (סמיכה), drink offerings (נסכים), and waving of the breast and thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and shows the real source behind the objection. "אם כבש" teaches that a leftover פסח is treated fully as a שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that has passed its first year can no longer be a פסח, and the ברייתא teaches that it is handled as a שלמים in every way. The same is true for שלמים that come because of a פסח. So this ברייתא already teaches the leftover פסח rule, and that makes the objection against רב נחמן's verse stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסח animal that is now over one year old and too old to be a פסח
Because of a פסח: coming from a פסח animal that was not used
Pressing hands on the animal's head before it is slaughtered
Flour, oil and wine offerings brought with the animal
Waving the breast and the thigh, which are later given to the כהן

steps.whatToRemember: There are now three possible sources for the rule that a leftover פסח becomes a שלמים: רב נחמן's "צאן ובקר", אבוה דשמואל's "אם מן הצאן", and the ברייתא's "אם כבש". This raises the question of why one rule needs three sources. Step 7 answers it: each source teaches a different case.
steps.whyThisMatters: In practice, a leftover פסח is treated like a regular שלמים in every way: it needs סמיכה, נסכים, and waving of the breast and thigh.

phrases.english: When it says: "If a lamb"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:7

phrases.english: this comes to include a Paschal offering whose year has passed,
and peace offerings that come because of a Paschal offering,
in all the laws of peace offerings:
that they require pressing hands on the head,
and drink offerings, and waving of the breast and thigh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא started in step 4, which supports the objection.
steps.raayaObject: That the leftover פסח rule is already learned from "אם כבש", not from "צאן ובקר".
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on ויקרא 3:7 that includes a פסח whose year has passed, and שלמים brought because of a פסח, in all the laws of שלמים.

steps.title: The ברייתא ends: a goat does not need the fat tail
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes: the words "ואם עז" break off the topic, which teaches that a goat offering does not need its אליה burned on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the פסוק says "And if a goat", it breaks off the topic. This teaches that a goat does not need its fat tail offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from the last step. It ends with a side point: the rule of the אליה is only for sheep, not goats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules of the אליה are written about a sheep, a כבש. The Torah then starts a new section with "ואם עז", which shows the אליה rule does not carry over to goats. With this ending, the ברייתא is a full third source that a leftover פסח is brought as a שלמים, and that sets up the problem of having three sources for one rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It broke off the topic. A new section starts, so the earlier rule does not carry over.
A goat

phrases.english: When it says "And if a goat"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:12

phrases.english: it broke off the topic,
teaching about the goat
that it does not require the fat tail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in steps 4 and 5. With the ברייתא complete, the problem of three sources for one rule is now fully in place.
steps.raayaObject: That the rule of the אליה is only for sheep, and that the ברייתא is a full third source for the leftover פסח rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The break in the פסוקים at "ואם עז" (ויקרא 3:12)

steps.title: Three sources for three different cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there really are three sources, and each one teaches a different kind of leftover פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three פסוקים are written. One is for a פסח whose time has passed and whose first year has also passed. One is for a פסח whose time has passed but whose year has not passed. One is for a פסח whose time has not passed and whose year has not passed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem of having three sources for one rule. It says each source covers a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח animal must be in its first year, and it has a set day, ערב פסח. The גמרא sets out three cases: both the day and the year have passed, only the day has passed, or neither has passed. Each of the three sources teaches that the animal is brought as a שלמים in one of these cases, so none of them is extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Three פסוקים, here the three sources from the earlier steps
Its time has passed. The day for bringing the פסח is over.
Its year has passed. The animal is older than one year, which is too old for a פסח.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up "time" and "year". זמנו means the day of the offering, ערב פסח. שנתו means the age of the animal, its first year of life.

phrases.english: Three verses are written:
one for where its time has passed
and its year has passed,
and one for where its time has passed
but its year has not passed,
phrases.notes: So the animal is still young enough to be a פסח, but its day is over.

phrases.english: and one for where its time has not passed
and its year has not passed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges of steps 3 and 4, which said the פסוק of step 2 is not needed because other sources already teach the rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources across different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All three sources teach the same single rule, so two of them are extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each source teaches the rule for a different case of a leftover פסח.

steps.title: Why the first case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to show why all three are needed. From the case where both the time and the year have passed, we could not learn the case where the animal is still good for פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all three are needed. If the תורה had taught us only the case where its time and its year have passed, I would say that is because the animal was pushed away completely. But where its time has passed and its year has not, it is still fit for פסח שני, so I would say no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a צריכותא, an explanation of why each source is needed. Here it shows the first case could not teach the second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal past both its day and its first year can never be a פסח again, so of course it becomes a שלמים. An animal past its day but still in its first year could still be offered on פסח שני. So we might think it should be saved for that and not turned into a שלמים, which is why a separate source is needed for it.

keyTerms.meaning: They are needed. This opens an explanation of why each source is necessary.
It was pushed away, meaning disqualified from being a פסח
The second פסח, a make-up date one month later
I would say no, the rule does not apply here

phrases.english: And they are needed,
for if it had taught us only
where its time has passed and its year has passed,
that is because it was pushed away completely,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל עִבְּרָה זְמַנּוֹ וְלֹא עִבְּרָה שְׁנָתוֹ,
phrases.english: but where its time has passed and its year has not passed,
which is fit for the second Pesach,
I would say no.
phrases.notes: Meaning: I would think it does not become a שלמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up step 7 by showing the first case could not teach the second.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא, explaining why each source is necessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the case where both the time and the year have passed, we could learn all the other cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: That case is easier, because the animal is fully disqualified. An animal still fit for פסח שני needs its own source.

steps.title: Why the second case alone would not be enough, so all three are needed
steps.stepSummary: From the case where only the time has passed, we could not learn the case where the animal is still fit for the first פסח. So all three sources are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had taught us only the case where its time has passed but its year has not, I would say that is because it was pushed away from the first פסח. But where neither its time nor its year has passed, it is still fit even for the first פסח, so I would say no. That is why all three are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא. It shows the second case could not teach the third, and concludes that every source is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal past its day has at least lost the first פסח, so turning it into a שלמים makes some sense. An animal whose day has not yet come could still be used for the regular פסח. So we might think it should not become a שלמים, and that is why the third source is needed. This closes the answer to the challenges of steps 3 and 4.

keyTerms.meaning: The first פסח, the regular offering on ערב פסח
It is fit or usable
It is needed. This closes the explanation: every source teaches something new.

steps.whatToRemember: There are three sources that a leftover פסח becomes a שלמים, and each covers a different case: (1) both the time and the year have passed; (2) only the time has passed; (3) neither has passed. Each case is less obvious than the one before it, so each one needs its own source.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only
where its time has passed and its year has not passed,
that is because it was pushed away from the first Pesach,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא עִבְּרָה זְמַנּוֹ וְלֹא עִבְּרָה שְׁנָתוֹ,
phrases.english: but where neither its time nor its year has passed,
which is fit even for the first Pesach,
I would say no,
so it is needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן עִבְּרָה זְמַנּוֹ וְלֹא עִבְּרָה שְׁנָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the צריכותא begun in step 8 with the second comparison, then closes with צריכא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: None of the three sources is extra. Each one teaches the שלמים rule for a different kind of leftover פסח.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק התודה היתה באה
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marks the end of the פרק about the תודה and related offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק "התודה היתה באה."
steps.whatsHappening: The פרק about the תודה offering has finished. This line is the traditional goodbye to the פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying הדרן shows that the discussion of leftover פסח animals and the תודה is complete. Everything after this line belongs to a new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: "We will return to you": the formula said when finishing a פרק
The name of the פרק that just ended, taken from its opening words

phrases.english: We will return to you,
"The thanks offering would come."
phrases.notes: A פרק is named by its first words, and these are the first words of the פרק we just finished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the perek right after the conclusion that all three sources are needed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק התודה היתה באה is complete.

steps.title: Grain for offerings may come from anywhere, except the עומר and שתי הלחם
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק's משנה rules that grain for communal and individual offerings may come from inside or outside ארץ ישראל, and from new or old grain. The עומר and שתי הלחם are the exceptions: they must come from new grain grown in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: All communal and individual offerings may come from ארץ ישראל or from outside it, and from new grain or old grain. The exceptions are the עומר and the שתי הלחם, which come only from new grain and only from ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה. It sets a general rule about where the grain for offerings may come from, and then names two exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule is easygoing: location and the age of the grain do not matter. The עומר and שתי הלחם are different, because they are tied to the new harvest. So they must be from this year's crop, from the land.

keyTerms.meaning: Communal offerings, brought on behalf of all of כלל ישראל
An individual: offerings brought by one person
New grain from this year's crop / old grain from earlier years
The barley offering brought on ט״ז ניסן
The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות

steps.confusionAlert: The "offerings" in this משנה are grain offerings (מנחות), not animal offerings. That is why it talks about new and old crops.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule for the whole new פרק. The גמרא will soon ask whether "only from the new" means an עומר from old grain is actually invalid.

phrases.english: MISHNA: All communal offerings
phrases.notes: This means grain offerings. That is why the משנה goes on to talk about crops.

phrases.english: and individual ones come from the Land
and from outside the Land,
from the new crop and from the old,
except for the עומר and the two loaves,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵינָן בָּאִין אֶלָּא מִן הֶחָדָשׁ וּמִן הָאָרֶץ.
phrases.english: which come only from the new crop and from the Land.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל קׇרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּיבּוּר וְהַיָּחִיד בָּאִין מִן הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new perek after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grain for מנחות may come from anywhere and from any year's crop. The עומר and שתי הלחם must come from new grain grown in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Offerings should use the best grain, but grain from any region is valid
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that all מנחות should come from top-quality grain. It names מכמס and זונחא as the best source for fine flour and עפוריים in the valley as second best. Grain from other regions is still valid; they simply preferred to bring it from these places.
steps.simpleTranslation: All of them come only from the best grain. Which grain is the best? מכמס and זונחא are first for fine flour, and second to them is עפוריים in the valley. All regions were valid, but this is where they would bring it from.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second rule: offerings should use the finest grain. It names the best places for that grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Only from the best" sounds strict. But the last line explains that other regions are valid too, so choosing these places is the best way to do the מצוה, not a requirement. This is a preference within the category of valid grain, not a rule that disqualifies other grain.

keyTerms.meaning: The choicest, best-quality grain
First, top rank (like the Greek letter alpha)
Fine flour used for מנחות
Second in rank
Valid, acceptable

steps.whatToRemember: The basic rule: grain from anywhere and any year is fine, except that the עומר and שתי הלחם need new grain from ארץ ישראל. They tried to use the best grain, from מכמס and זונחא and then עפוריים, but other grain is still valid.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read "only from the best" as meaning ordinary grain is invalid. The משנה itself says all regions were valid.

phrases.aramaic: וְכוּלָּן אֵינָן בָּאִין אֶלָּא מִן הַמּוּבְחָר,
phrases.english: And all of them come only from the choicest grain,
And which is the choicest for them?
Michmas and Zonecha —
phrases.notes: Some versions have the names in round brackets. The names in square brackets are the corrected wording.

phrases.english: are first for fine flour,
second to them is Aforayim in the valley.
All the regions were valid,
but from here they would bring it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלָּן אֵינָן בָּאִין אֶלָּא מִן הַמּוּבְחָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a second rule about grain quality and the preferred places to get it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every מנחה should use the best grain, first from מכמס and זונחא and then from עפוריים. Grain from any region is still valid.

steps.title: Our משנה disagrees with a ברייתא that allows old grain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that our משנה does not follow a תנא who says the עומר and שתי הלחם are valid even from old grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like this תנא. A ברייתא teaches: an עומר brought from old grain is valid, and שתי הלחם brought from old grain are valid. However, the person failed to do the מצוה in the best way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by saying our משנה, which demanded new grain, disagrees with a ברייתא that accepts old grain after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said the עומר and שתי הלחם must come from new grain. The ברייתא says new grain is only the proper way (לכתחילה). If old grain was used, the offering still counts (בדיעבד). This sets up the next steps, which find the פסוקים behind the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Old grain, from a previous year's crop
Valid; the offering counts
He missed part of the מצוה; it counts, but it was not done the ideal way
The barley offering brought on the second day of פסח
The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not say old grain is ideal. It agrees that new grain is the מצוה. It only says that old grain still works after the fact.

phrases.english: Gemara
Our Mishnah is not in line with this tanna,
phrases.notes: Our משנה said the עומר and שתי הלחם must come from new grain.

phrases.english: as it was taught in a baraita:
An omer that comes from old grain is valid,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם הַבָּאוֹת מִן הַיָּשָׁן – כְּשֵׁרוֹת,
phrases.english: two loaves that come from old grain are valid,
except that he has missed a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the new משנה's rule of 'new grain only' with a ברייתא that accepts old grain after the fact.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the ברייתא, an עומר or שתי הלחם from old grain is valid after the fact, though the מצוה was not done ideally.

steps.title: The פסוק source for an עומר from old grain
steps.stepSummary: The extra words 'תקריב את מנחת בכוריך' teach that the עומר is valid even from grain stored in the attic.
steps.simpleTranslation: The עומר: as it is written, 'you shall bring the מנחה of your first grain'. This teaches that it is valid even from grain stored in the attic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the פסוק behind the ברייתא's ruling that an עומר from old grain is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'תקריב את מנחת בכוריך' come after the פסוק has already described the offering. The extra words are read to include grain that sat in storage, meaning old grain. So the עומר is valid even from an old crop.

keyTerms.meaning: The offering of first grain, here meaning the עומר
An attic, where old grain was stored
'And even'; signals that the פסוק includes an extra case

phrases.english: The omer: as it is written,
"You shall bring the meal offering of your first fruits,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:14. These words are extra in the פסוק, so they teach something new.

phrases.english: and even from the attic.
phrases.notes: Grain kept in the attic is old grain from an earlier crop.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural basis for the first half of the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The ברייתא's ruling that an עומר from old grain is valid

steps.title: The פסוק source for שתי הלחם
steps.stepSummary: 'ממושבותיכם' teaches that the grain must come from ארץ ישראל and that even old grain is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: שתי הלחם: as it is written, 'From your dwellings you shall bring.' This means not from outside ארץ ישראל. 'From your dwellings' also means even from grain stored in the attic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the פסוק for שתי הלחם and draws two lessons from the word 'ממושבותיכם'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first lesson: 'your dwellings' means ארץ ישראל, so the grain cannot come from חוצה לארץ. The second lesson: anything from your dwellings counts, even old grain stored in the attic. Learning two lessons from one word sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From your dwellings'; read here as ארץ ישראל
Outside ארץ ישראל
'You shall bring', in the plural

phrases.english: The two loaves: as it is written:
"From your dwellings you shall bring,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:17

phrases.english: and not from outside of Eretz Yisrael.
"From your dwellings": and even from the attic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural basis for the second half of the ברייתא, parallel to the עומר.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that שתי הלחם must come from ארץ ישראל but may come from old grain

steps.title: One word cannot teach two lessons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: 'ממושבותיכם' was already used to teach 'only ארץ ישראל', so how can it also teach that old grain is allowed?
steps.simpleTranslation: But you already used up that word for a different lesson!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that the word 'ממושבותיכם' was already spent on the lesson about ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually one word in a פסוק teaches only one lesson. 'ממושבותיכם' already taught 'not from חוצה לארץ'. So the lesson about old grain needs a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But this'; opens a challenge
'You took it out', meaning you already used this word for another lesson
A lesson learned from the words of a פסוק

phrases.english: Didn't you already use it?
phrases.notes: He means you already used 'ממושבותיכם' to teach 'not from outside ארץ ישראל'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the double use of 'ממושבותיכם' in step 15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A word already used for one lesson (only ארץ ישראל) cannot also be the source for a second lesson (old grain allowed).

steps.title: The old-grain rule comes from 'תביאו'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the old-grain lesson comes from the next word, 'תביאו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'you shall bring'. This teaches: even from grain stored in the attic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by moving the old-grain lesson to a different word in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now each word teaches one thing. 'ממושבותיכם' teaches only grain from ארץ ישראל. 'תביאו' teaches that even old grain may be used. This removes the problem of one word teaching two lessons.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק
'You shall bring'; now the source for allowing old grain
A word in the פסוק that includes an extra case

phrases.english: The verse states: "You shall bring,"
phrases.notes: This is the next word in the same פסוק, ויקרא 23:17.

phrases.english: and even from the attic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 by finding a separate word for the old-grain lesson.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the lesson to a different word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both lessons come from 'ממושבותיכם', which seems to use one word twice.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ממושבותיכם' teaches only ארץ ישראל; 'תביאו' teaches that even old grain is allowed.

steps.title: But 'Bring' Is Already Needed for Another Lesson
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the word 'תביאו' is already used to teach a different law, so it cannot also teach that old grain is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this word is needed to teach that anything you bring from another place must be like this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 17. It says the word 'תביאו' is already busy teaching a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 17 the old-grain lesson was moved from 'ממושבותיכם' to 'תביאו'. Now the גמרא says 'תביאו' already teaches that what you bring from another place must match these loaves. One word normally cannot be used for two separate lessons, so the old-grain source seems to be gone again.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (a different lesson)
From another place
It is like this one

phrases.english: But this is needed for him,
that anything you bring from another place –
it is like this!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 17 by showing its source word is already used.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'תביאו' teaches old grain is allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'תביאו' is already needed for the lesson that what you bring from elsewhere must be like these loaves, so it is not free to teach another law.

steps.title: The Plural Form Teaches Two Lessons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תורה could have written 'תביא' but wrote 'תביאו', so the extra letter lets the word teach both lessons.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the verse write 'bring' in singular. Why does it say 'bring' in plural? Learn from it two things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Because the תורה used a longer form of the word than it needed, the word can teach two laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'תביאו' taught only one lesson, the shorter 'תביא' would have been enough. The extra letter shows the word has extra meaning. So it teaches both the 'from another place' lesson and that old grain is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the verse write
Learn from it two things

steps.whatToRemember: The source that old grain is allowed for the עומר and שתי הלחם survives: 'תביאו' teaches two lessons because of its extra letter.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse write 'bring' (singular),
what is 'bring' (plural)?
Learn from it two things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording in the פסוק allows a double lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'תביאו' can only teach one law, so old grain has no source.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plural form is extra, so 'תביאו' teaches both laws.

steps.title: But the תורה Says 'First'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view that old grain is valid, because the תורה calls these offerings 'ראשית', the first of the crop.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written 'first'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק that seems to say these offerings must come from the new crop. This challenges the view that old grain is acceptable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ראשית' means the first of the harvest. That sounds like the grain must be new. If so, how can the בריתא say old grain is valid?

keyTerms.meaning: First; the first of the crop

phrases.english: But isn't it written 'first'?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:10 for the עומר, and ויקרא 2:12 for the שתי הלחם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After securing the source for old grain, the גמרא raises a פסוק that seems to contradict it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the עומר and שתי הלחם are valid from old grain
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'ראשית' implies the offering must come from the new crop.

steps.title: 'First' Is Only the Ideal Way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'ראשית' only describes the best way to do the מצוה, not a requirement that makes the offering invalid if skipped.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is for the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in one word: 'ראשית' is למצוה. Using new grain is the proper way, but old grain still works after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a difference between the ideal way to do a מצוה and what is required for it to count. 'ראשית' teaches the ideal. It does not make old-grain offerings invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: For the ideal fulfillment of the מצוה, not a requirement

steps.confusionAlert: 'למצוה' does not mean the law is unimportant. It means you should do it this way, but if you didn't, the offering still counts.

phrases.english: For the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the פסוק to the ideal, not to what is required
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ראשית' means only new grain is valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ראשית' is only the ideal; old grain is still valid.

steps.title: But the תורה Says 'New'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again with the word 'חדשה' written about the שתי הלחם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it written 'new'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second word that seems to require new grain. This is a stronger challenge, because it adds to 'ראשית'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שתי הלחם are called 'מנחה חדשה', a new meal offering. Together with 'ראשית', the תורה seems to say new grain twice. That suggests it is a real requirement and not just the ideal way.

keyTerms.meaning: New

phrases.english: Isn't it written 'new'?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:16

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After 'ראשית' was explained as למצוה, the גמרא brings another word to push the challenge further.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the שתי הלחם are valid from old grain
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'חדשה' plainly means new grain, and saying it again suggests it is required.

steps.title: 'New' Means First of All the Meal Offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'חדשה' teaches something else: the שתי הלחם must be the first offering from the new crop, as רבי נתן and רבי עקיבא say in a בריתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is needed for what was taught: רבי נתן and רבי עקיבא said, the two loaves that come from old grain are valid. And how do I explain 'new'? That it should be new for all the meal offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'חדשה' does not require new grain. It brings a בריתא showing it teaches that the שתי הלחם come before every other מנחה from the new crop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן and רבי עקיבא rule that the שתי הלחם are valid from old grain. So they explain 'חדשה' differently: it is the first מנחה brought from the new crop. Since the word is used for this lesson, it cannot prove old grain is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: The two loaves brought on שבועות
The old grain, from a previous year
How do I explain (this word)?
Valid

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the בריתא's view, that old grain is valid, has strong backing from רבי נתן and רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: This is needed for that which is taught:
Rabbi Natan and Rabbi Akiva said:
The two loaves that come from the old –
are valid,
and how do I fulfill 'new'?
That it should be new for all the meal offerings.
phrases.notes: He means it is the first מנחה brought from the new crop, before any others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirects the פסוק to a different lesson, backed by a בריתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'חדשה' means the שתי הלחם must be from new grain.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'חדשה' means the שתי הלחם are the first מנחה from the new crop; old grain is still valid.

steps.title: Limiting the Argument to New Grain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to define the exact scope of the מחלוקת: they only argue about whether new grain is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until here they only disagree about new grain,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It starts to pin down that the משנה and the בריתא only argue about whether new grain is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having defended the בריתא, the גמרא now limits the argument to one issue: new grain. This suggests that on other points, which will come next, both sides may agree.

keyTerms.meaning: They only disagree up to here
New grain, from this year's crop

phrases.english: Until here they do not disagree
except regarding new grain,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the בריתא, the גמרא turns to defining the limits of the מחלוקת with the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה and the בריתא disagree only about whether the עומר and שתי הלחם must be from new grain.
